{{nihongo|'''Isobe inamura Shrine'''|礒部稲村神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

'''Isobe Inamura Shrine''' (いそべいなむらじんじゃ) is a shrine in {{ill|Sakuragawa, Ibaraki|ar|ساكوراغاوا (إيباراكي)|azb|ساکوراقاوا، ایباراکی|ce|Сакурагава|ceb|Sakuragawa (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Sakuragawa|eo|Sakuragaŭa|es|Sakuragawa (Ibaraki)|fa|ساکوراگاوا، ایباراکی|fi|Sakuragawa|fr|Sakuragawa|gl|Sakuragawa|id|Sakuragawa, Ibaraki|it|Sakuragawa|ja|桜川市|ko|사쿠라가와시|mzn|ساکوراگاوا، ایباراکی|nl|Sakuragawa|pl|Sakuragawa|pt|Sakuragawa|ro|Sakuragawa|ru|Сакурагава|sv|Sakuragawa|tl|Sakuragawa, Ibaraki|tr|Sakuragawa|tt|Сакурагава|uk|Сакураґава|ur|ساکورا گاوا، ایباراکی|uz|Sakuragava (Ibaraki)|vi|Sakuragawa, Ibaraki|war|Sakuragawa, Ibaraki|zh|櫻川市|zh_classical|櫻川市|zh_min_nan|Sakuragawa-chhī|zh_yue|櫻川|qid=Q990350}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|Q83273|qid=Q83273}}, enshrining deities including {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amateru-sume-Okami}}. Its former name was Isobe Inamura-no-miya. It is a shikinaisha small shrine of Niihari District, {{ill|Hitachi Province|cs|Provincie Hitači|de|Provinz Hitachi|es|Provincia de Hitachi|fa|ولایت هیتاچی|fr|Province de Hitachi|gl|Provincia de Hitachi|hak|Hitachi-koet|id|Provinsi Hitachi|it|Hitachi (provincia)|ja|常陸国|ko|히타치국|lt|Hitačio žemė|nl|Hitachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Hitachi|ru|Хитати (провинция)|simple|Hitachi Province|sk|Hitači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Хитачи|tr|Hitachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Хітаті|zh|常陸國|zh_min_nan|Hitati-kok|zh_yue|常陸國|qid=Q1055353}}. Its former rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}<ref name="annai">Ibaraki Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines: [http://www.ibaraki-jinjacho.jp/ibaraki/kensei/jinja/03054.html Isobe Inamura Shrine], viewed July 10, 2019.</ref>.

Centered on the shrine approach, part of the precinct and part of adjacent {{ill|Isobe Sakuragawa Park|Q130458624|qid=Q130458624}} are designated as the national scenic site "Sakuragawa" (designated {{ill|1924|Q2173|qid=Q2173}}) and as the national natural monument "{{ill|Cherry trees of Sakuragawa|Q55525177|qid=Q55525177}}" (designated {{ill|1974|Q2478|qid=Q2478}})<ref>{{Cite journal |和書 |url=https://www.nat.museum.ibk.ed.jp/assets/data/materials/research/report/21/p081-90.pdf |author1=Toshio Katsuki|author2=Takeo Hinata|author3=Yuji Watanabe|author4=Ryo Isobe|author5=Takuya Yamakawa|title=Cherry varieties of nationally designated scenic/natural monument sites in Sakuragawa City, Ibaraki |journal=Bulletin of the Ibaraki Nature Museum |issue=21 |publisher=Ibaraki Nature Museum |year=2018 |pages=81-89}}</ref>.

=== History ===
Tradition says that in October of {{ill|AD 111|Q30640|qid=Q30640}} ({{ill|Emperor Keikō|Q329723|qid=Q329723}} year 40), {{ill|Yamato Takeru|lt=Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258}} transferred and enshrined {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Iso-no-miya}}, an {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|Q2859485|qid=Q2859485}} of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}.

In {{ill|849|Q23902|qid=Q23902}} ({{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} 2), during floods or drought, a rain-prayer rite was conducted at Kagami-ga-ike in the Yamaguchi settlement, Iwase Town. In {{ill|939|Q23422|qid=Q23422}} ({{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} 2), {{ill|Taira no Sadamori|Q3514057|qid=Q3514057}} prayed here for success in suppressing {{ill|Taira no Masakado|Q1207652|qid=Q1207652}}. From the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} onward, the {{ill|Ōnakatomi clan|Q11431853|qid=Q11431853}}, who were priests of {{ill|Katori Jingū|Q372380|qid=Q372380}} ({{ill|Katori, Chiba|Q858357|qid=Q858357}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}}), administered the shrine lands and sacred territory<ref>Ancient document of {{ill|Enrico De Nicola|Q1245|qid=Q1245}} ({{ill|Kangen|Q1194187|qid=Q1194187}} 3), held by {{ill|Kashima Jingū|Q706499|qid=Q706499}}</ref>.

In {{ill|1429|Q6326|qid=Q6326}} ({{ill|Eikyō|Q1193059|qid=Q1193059}} 1), {{ill|Ashikaga Mochiuji|Q4805073|qid=Q4805073}} of the {{ill|Kantō kubō|Q860777|qid=Q860777}} donated 25 kanmon (equivalent to 230 koku) as shrine land. In Eikyo 10 ({{ill|1438|Q6377|qid=Q6377}}), shrine priest Isobe Sukeyuki presented one volume of the hanami tale ''Sakurago Monogatari'' to Mochiuji. Seeing that story, the 6th shogun {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshinori|Q239170|qid=Q239170}} had {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Zeami Motokiyo}} compose the Noh play "{{ill|Sakuragawa|Q136744837|qid=Q136744837|lt=Sakuragawa}}"<ref>From the shrine noticeboard.</ref>. In {{ill|1585|Q6736|qid=Q6736}} ({{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 13), shrine lands were confiscated by the {{ill|Yūki clan|Q2975399|qid=Q2975399}} during Kanto warfare, but in the early {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was protected by the {{ill|Inoue clan|Q2975275|qid=Q2975275}}, and {{ill|Emperor Go-Mizunoo|Q320229|qid=Q320229}} granted a calligraphy plaque for {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isobe Daimyojin}} (still extant). In {{ill|1696|Q7699|qid=Q7699}} ({{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 9), {{ill|Naitō Masatomo|Q10514812|qid=Q10514812}}, lord of {{ill|Akanuma Domain|Q10863285|qid=Q10863285}} in {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}, donated 15 koku 2 to 5 sho 2 go as shrine land.

=== Shrine names ===
Since ancient times the shrine has been called Isobe-no-miya, Isobe Inamura-no-miya, Sakuragawa Myojin, Isobe Daimyojin, Inamura Shrine, and Sakuragawa Isobe Inamura Shrine. Documents related to Hitachi Saidaisha Inada-hime Shrine (held at Hitachi Kokubunji Gokuraku-ji) list it as Isobe Inamura-no-miya in Niihari District, one of the 28 Hitachi shrines (Engishiki shrines).
